statements.t: We expect our business to be affected by the below - described key trends and uncertainties.
To the extent our underlying assumptions about, or interpretations of, available information prove incorrect, our actual results may vary materially from expected results.

To address the risks posed by fluctuating commodity prices, we intend to continue evaluating the relevant price environments and adjust our capital spending plans to reflect our customers’ anticipated activity levels, while maintaining appropriate liquidity and financial flexibility.
However, we expect our cost of capital to remain competitive, as our peers face similar interest-rate dynamics.

We utilize DCF as a measure of the operating performance of our asset base and as such reconcile it to net income (loss) and Adjusted EBITDA, with the adjustments intended to enhance period-over-period comparability.

The timing and amount of purchases under the program will be determined based on ongoing assessments of capital needs, our financial performance, the market price of our common units, and other factors, including organic growth and acquisition opportunities and general market conditions.

We expect our exposure to the concentrated risk of non - payment or non - performance to continue for as long as our commercial relationships with Occidental generate a significant portion of our revenues.

The preparation of consolidated financial statements in accordance with GAAP requires management to make informed judgments and estimates that affect the amounts of assets and liabilities as of the date of the financial statements and the amounts of revenues and expenses recognized during the periods reported.

statements.t: “The Brazos integration is progressing as expected, and we anticipate tying those assets into our West Texas Complex by mid-December, enabling us to reduce offloads and generate more value for WES unitholders.”

“With a greater number of wells expected to come online relative to the third quarter, we expect strong fourth-quarter results and anticipate full-year Adjusted EBITDA above the midpoint of our guidance range of $2.750 billion to $2.950 billion.

This represents an increase of more than $250.0 million relative to the $2.600 billion midpoint of our original Adjusted EBITDA guidance range announced in February, or more than $150.0 million above the midpoint excluding the Brazos acquisition.

We also expect 2026 capital expenditures to be slightly above the high end of our $850.0 million to $1.0 billion guidance range, reflecting our investment in Solitude and accelerating producer activity levels.”

“We expect this momentum to carry into 2027, with incremental customer activity, a full year of contribution from Brazos, the start-up of the Pathfinder pipeline, North Loving II coming online, and new gathering and processing agreements in the Powder River Basin positioning us for throughput growth across all three product lines again next year.

We expect 2027 capital expenditures to be relatively in line with 2026, with approximately 80-percent directed to the Delaware Basin, our largest growth driver, which includes our investment in the Solitude pipeline and completion of North Loving II.

We utilize DCF as a measure of the operating performance of our asset base and as such reconcile it to net income (loss) and Adjusted EBITDA, with the adjustments intended to enhance period-over-period comparability.

dropped.t: “WES delivered record Adjusted EBITDA of $736.5 million in the second quarter, an increase of 8-percent sequentially and 19-percent compared to the prior-year period, and based on the strength of our first-half results, the Brazos Delaware acquisition, and continued elevated commodity prices, we are raising the mid-points of our full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, Distributable Cash Flow, and Free Cash Flow guidance…

“Looking to the remainder of the year, the higher commodity-price environment has incentivized many of our Delaware Basin producing customers to increase activity levels in the second half of 2026, which is expected to position WES for stronger Delaware Basin natural-gas and produced-water throughput growth in 2027.
Reflecting the contribution from the Brazos Delaware acquisition and the most recent production forecasts from our customers, WES is revising its full-year 2026 guidance as follows:

• Reiterating full-year distribution guidance of at least $3.70 per unit (7) , which includes distributions to be paid in calendar-year 2026, and implies a current annualized run-rate of $3.72 per unit based on our prior quarter distribution of $0.93 per unit.

“An exceptionally strong first half of the year and the completed Brazos Delaware acquisition give us the confidence to raise our full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, Distributable Cash Flow, and Free Cash Flow guidance ranges,” commented Kristen Shults, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.
“With the inclusion of Brazos Delaware and throughput outperformance across the portfolio, we now expect natural-gas throughput to increase by mid-single digits average year-over-year in 2026.
“We now expect 2026 capital expenditures to be toward the high end of our guidance range of $850 million to $1.0 billion.
